_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench check`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

example.quote: CLRS Figure 22.3: the undirected graph on

meanings.init: The search starts from the source alone, discovered at distance 0.

tensorNotes.G: the graph: an entry of 1 is an edge, stored in both directions
tensorNotes.F: the frontier: the distance of each vertex discovered in this generation
tensorNotes.T: candidate distances one hop beyond the frontier
tensorNotes.ParentCand: frontier edges into newly discovered vertices
tensorNotes.NewParent: the parent edge chosen for each newly discovered vertex
tensorNotes.Parent: the BFS tree so far: an entry s,d means pi(d) = s

E01.graph: Every frontier vertex offers each neighbour a distance one more than its own.
E01.einsum: Add $G_{s,d}$ to $F_{i,s}$ where both are present, and take the minimum over $s$.

E02.graph: Only white vertices are discovered; they form the next frontier.

E03.graph: An edge from the frontier into a newly discovered vertex could be its parent edge.
E03.einsum: Keep $G_{s,d}$ where $s$ is on the frontier and $d$ was just discovered.

E04.graph: Each newly discovered vertex takes one of its candidate parents; which one is free.

E05.graph: The new parent edges join the BFS tree.
E05.einsum: Take $NewParent$ where present, else carry $Parent_{i}$ forward.

E06.graph: Newly discovered vertices are no longer white.
E06.einsum: OR $P_{i,d}$ with $F_{i+1,d}$ wherever either is present.

E07.graph: Newly discovered vertices keep their distance.
E07.einsum: Take $F_{i+1,d}$ where present, else carry $Depth_{i,d}$ forward.

stop.graph: Stop when a level discovers nothing.
stop.einsum: Halt when $F_{i+1}$ has no non-empty entries.
